question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}4 & 16 & -8 \\ -3 & -12 & 6 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}4 & 16 & -8 \\ -3 & -12 & 6 \end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 4 & -2 \\ -3 & -12 & 6 \end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The system corresponding to $M$ is 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+3y &=-4\\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+3y=-4.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=-3y-4,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-3y-4\\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\  y \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} -3y-4 \\  y \end{bmatrix}=⟨-3y-4,y⟩,\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

question.:question/problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & 9 & 9 \\ 2 & 6 & 6 \end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 3 & 3 \\ 2 & 6 & 6 \end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 3 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+3y &=3\\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+3y=3.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=3-3y\\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\  y \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 3-3y \\  y \end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
